cards.text: Isaiah, God's prophet, has been warning about mighty Assyria. Now he looks ahead to 'that day,' when only a remnant of Israel is left, a handful of survivors from the house of Jacob. And on that day, something changes about who they lean on.

cards.question: On that day, the remnant of Israel will keep depending on the one who struck them.
So on that day, who will the remnant of Israel truly rely on?

answers.text: The LORD the Holy One of Israel

cards.text: Then Isaiah says it plain: 'A remnant will return—a remnant of Jacob—to the Mighty God.' A remnant is the leftover dough after the cutting's done, and friend, don't you DARE laugh at the scraps, because some of my best cookies ever came out of the scraps.

cards.question: Isaiah says that even if Israel's people are like the sand of the sea, all of them will return.

cards.text: Then comes a heavy word. Destruction has been decreed, overflowing with righteousness, and it's coming on the whole land.

cards.question: Who does Isaiah say will carry out the destruction decreed on the whole land?

cards.text: So the Lord GOD of Hosts speaks to His people who live in Zion. Assyria is striking them with a rod and lifting a staff against them, the way the Egyptians did.

cards.question: What does the Lord tell His people in Zion about Assyria?
The Lord tells His people in Zion not to fear, because in just a little while His fury against them will ___.

cards.text: His anger turns to their destruction, and the LORD of Hosts will brandish a whip against them, like when He struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. Assyria's been swinging that rod around this WHOLE time, and now, real quiet, somebody else picks up the whip.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts will also raise His staff over the sea. Isaiah says it will be like what He did where?

answers.text: What He did at Mount Carmel

cards.text: On that day, the burden comes off their shoulders and the yoke comes off their neck. Friend, I spent YEARS with a stack of old takeout menus sitting on top of me, so believe me, I know what it feels like when the weight finally comes off.

cards.question: Isaiah says the yoke will be broken because their ___ will be too large.

cards.text: Now Isaiah shows Assyria on the march. They go into Aiath, through Migron, and store their supplies at Michmash, and it's like watching a delivery tracker move town by town, except NOBODY wants this package.

cards.question: Assyria crosses at the ford and says they'll spend the night at Geba. How does the town of Ramah react?

cards.text: Gibeah of Saul flees, the Daughter of Gallim is told to cry aloud, Madmenah flees, and the people of Gebim take refuge. Town after town, one after another, like dominoes.

cards.question: With towns fleeing one after another, Isaiah says the Assyrian army will halt at Nob.
From Nob, the Assyrians shake a fist at the hill of which city?

cards.text: So there's Assyria at Nob, shaking a fist at Jerusalem, and then Isaiah says, 'Behold.' The Lord GOD of Hosts steps in, and the picture turns into a forest of tall, lofty trees.

cards.question: With terrifying power, the Lord GOD of Hosts lops off the branches and leaves the tall, lofty trees ___.

cards.text: He clears the forest thickets with an axe. I've chopped a LOT of cookie dough in my day, friend, and I have never once swung like that.

cards.question: In Isaiah's picture, Lebanon stands firm before the Mighty One.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 4 has a dash outside a quotation: "Then Isaiah says it plain: 'A remnant will return—a remnant of Jacob—to the Mighty God.' A remnant is the leftover dough after the cutting's done, and friend, don't you DARE laugh at the scraps, because some of my best cookies ever came out of the scraps."

rule.text: No em dashes or en dashes to make a sentence longer.

findings.problem: The setup line 'something changes about who they lean on' tells the baker the remnant won't keep depending on the one who struck them. That gives away card 2, which then can only be False.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'only a remnant of Israel is left, a handful of survivors' goes beyond the text. Verse 20 says 'the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob.' It never says 'handful', and the 'only' comes from verse 22, outside this card's citation.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: 'Isaiah, God's prophet, has been warning about mighty Assyria' is a Bible fact from the earlier passage (Isaiah 10:5-19), but it has no reference. The card cites only Isaiah 10:20.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Card 1 ('only a remnant of Israel is left') and card 4 ('A remnant will return') have already told the baker that only a remnant returns. That gives away the answer to 'all of them will return' before the card asks it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'A remnant is the leftover dough after the cutting's done' spends card words defining the hard word 'remnant', which the dictionary pop-up covers.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The right answer 'The LORD the Holy One of Israel' is a full Bible title, while the wrong answers 'The king of Egypt' and 'The king of Babylon' are plain. The right answer stands out as the most Bible-sounding.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Midian appears here for the first time but isn't introduced. The card doesn't say simply who they are.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 13, right before it, says 'the yoke comes off their neck'. That gives away 'neck' as the blank's answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke 'I've chopped a LOT of cookie dough in my day' doesn't click right away. People don't chop cookie dough, and Papa Dorin is a stamper. The comparison to swinging an axe doesn't share the same action.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
